articles.title: Mumbai Weather: City Sizzles at 37.3°C, 3.8 Degrees Above Normal; Pune Likely to See 35°C on Tuesday - Lokmat Times
articles.full_text:
Mumbai recorded Maharashtra’s highest maximum temperature at 37.3 degrees Celsius on Monday, October 19, which was 3.8 degrees above normal, according to the India Meteorological Department (IMD). Solapur followed closely at 37.2 degrees Celsius, 4.2 degrees above normal. Above-normal temperatures continued across several parts of the state, while most weather stations reported no rainfall. In Mumbai City, the minimum temperature was 27.4 degrees Celsius, 2.2 degrees above normal. The IMD has forecast a maximum temperature of around 35 degrees Celsius in Pune on Tuesday, with partly cloudy conditions likely later in the day.
Mumbai and Konkan see temperatures above normal
At Mumbai’s Santacruz weather station, which represents the suburbs, the maximum temperature was 37.1 degrees Celsius, 3.1 degrees above normal. The minimum stood at 25.4 degrees Celsius, 1.5 degrees above normal. Alibag recorded a maximum of 36.4 degrees Celsius and a minimum of 28.2 degrees Celsius, with the minimum 4.5 degrees above normal. Dahanu also recorded a maximum of 36.4 degrees Celsius, 2.7 degrees above normal. Ratnagiri registered 34.3 degrees Celsius, while Panjim recorded 34 degrees Celsius.
Solapur, Jalgaon and Pune record high temperatures
In Madhya Maharashtra, Solapur recorded the state’s second-highest maximum temperature at 37.2 degrees Celsius. Jalgaon registered 36.4 degrees Celsius, while Ahilyanagar recorded 36 degrees Celsius. Satara’s maximum temperature reached 35.2 degrees Celsius, 3.6 degrees above normal. Pune’s Shivajinagar station recorded 35.1 degrees Celsius, 3.5 degrees above normal, while Lohgaon registered 34.4 degrees Celsius. Malegaon and Nashik also recorded 34.4 degrees Celsius. Sangli registered 33.9 degrees Celsius and Kolhapur recorded 33.1 degrees Celsius. Mahabaleshwar’s minimum temperature was 19 degrees Celsius, 2.5 degrees above normal.
Amravati and Buldhana among warm locations in Vidarbha
Amravati recorded a maximum temperature of 36.6 degrees Celsius, 4.1 degrees above normal, while Akola registered 36.3 degrees Celsius. Buldhana recorded 35.2 degrees Celsius, which was 4.9 degrees above normal, the highest departure from normal among the maximum temperatures listed in the bulletin. Washim registered 36 degrees Celsius and Chandrapur recorded 35.6 degrees Celsius. Yavatmal and Wardha recorded maximum temperatures of 34.8 degrees Celsius and 35 degrees Celsius, respectively. Nagpur registered 34.2 degrees Celsius, while Bramhapuri recorded 34.1 degrees Celsius. Gondia’s minimum temperature was 19.4 degrees Celsius, 1.2 degrees below normal.
Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar records 36 degrees Celsius
In Marathwada, Chhatrapati Sambhajinagar recorded a maximum temperature of 36 degrees Celsius, 4.2 degrees above normal. Parbhani registered 35 degrees Celsius, 2.5 degrees above normal, while Beed recorded 34.7 degrees Celsius, 3.4 degrees above normal. Dharashiv recorded a maximum of 34.2 degrees Celsius, 2.9 degrees above normal. The IMD bulletin also reported above-normal minimum temperatures at several stations in the region.
Pune weather forecast for Tuesday
The IMD has forecast mainly clear skies in Pune on Tuesday, with partly cloudy conditions likely to develop towards the afternoon or evening. The maximum temperature is expected to be around 35 degrees Celsius, while the minimum is likely to be around 22 degrees Celsius. On Monday, Pune’s Shivajinagar station recorded a maximum of 35.1 degrees Celsius and a minimum of 22.1 degrees Celsius. These were 3.5 degrees and 3.4 degrees above normal, respectively.
Pune rainfall remains below normal
Pune recorded no rainfall on Monday. Its seasonal rainfall stood at 1.4 mm, compared with the normal of 62.9 mm, leaving a deficit of 61.5 mm. The IMD’s evening bulletin showed that most reporting stations across Maharashtra remained dry on Monday, even as temperatures stayed above normal in several areas.
